rulings.correct_value: A methods and standardisation study by a working group: a calibration that linearly scales the outcome of any amyloid PET analysis method or tracer onto a 0 to 100 'Centiloid' (CL) scale anchored at the mean of young controls (0) and the mean of typical Alzheimer's disease patients (100). The process has three levels: Level-1 defines the standard method and the anchor points; Level-2 is how an independent site calibrates its own tracer or method to the scale; Level-3 is exact reproduction of an already-calibrated method as a pipeline check.
rulings.quote: There are three “levels” to the Centiloid process. The first level is described in this report and need not be repeated by other sites. The purpose of this level-1 process is to set the “typical” 0-anchor and 100-anchor points for all future scaling operations. The second level of the Centiloid process is the method suggested for individual sites to scale their unique method of PiB-PET or any method using a tracer other than PiB to the Centiloid scale. The third level is to be used when an individual site simply wants to exactly reproduce a method that has previously been scaled to Centiloids and is basically a check of the processing pipeline to ensure that errors are eliminated before the processing and scaling of site-collected data is begun.
rulings.reasoning: The document states the design directly — a working group scaling each method or tracer to a 0-100 scale anchored by young controls and typical AD patients — and then defines the three levels exactly as reading B describes, so the field is not empty.
